main_text.p: Legem habet Demosthenes [illegible, ~14 letters] Ae[?]σχ[?]ινην, qua consulitur vitæ eo-rum, qui siue cum primam apud Areopagitas iudices habuerant orationem, siue sua sponte, conscij sibi cædis humanæ, vltroneum amplectebantur exi-lium, relicta patria, & Laribus. Hos igitur occidi vetat Legislator, aut mortis eorum causam præbere: quippe nihil interest, inquit Vlpianus Libro VIII. ad Legem Iuliam & Papiam, occidat quis, an causam mortis præbeat. Lege XV. D. ad Legem Corneliam de sicarijs: Hos igitur occidi non vult Draco, dummodo, foro, vrbis territorio, sacris, certaminibusque publicis abstineant. Excidere certe occisi patria ius est & æquum: at quæ, malum, inuidia est aliena consi-stere terra? Demosthenes ibidem: [illegible, ~30 letters] [illegible, ~40 letters] [illegible, ~30 letters].

page.notes: Greek text is printed in a worn Greek type and is only partly legible at this scan resolution; Greek passages I could not read letter by letter are marked illegible rather than guessed. Latin text in the italic column and the Latin paragraphs is clear. The final line is cut off at the foot of the scan and ends in a partial Greek word. The Greek capitals in the left parallel column were read with reasonable confidence, but their accents and breathings are not fully certain.
